item.description: SPRINGFIELD — Missouri State (1-0) women’s basketball started the new season with a bang on Monday, Nov. 2. The Lady Bears defeated in-state opponent Southeast Missouri State 77-40. Prior to the game, a new banner was unveiled honoring Missouri State’s Conference USA Tournament title. Here are some takeaways from Missouri State's opening night victory. Lady Bears' depth was a huge factor Missouri State had 13 different scorers against SeMo. Lainie Douglas led the Lady Bears' offense. She scored 15 points on 6-for-9 shooting. Kaemyn Bekemeier added 11 points, too. The two leaders were the only players to reach double figures. "I thought we had a ton of balance across the board," head coach Beth Cunningham said. "The strength of our team can certainly be our depth and versatility. I think we showed that tonight." The team interchanged lineups often, showcasing the team's depth. This is an area the Lady Bears think will be very impactful this season, especially as games continue to stack. "It was a great team win," Douglas said. "We fed off of each other and the energy was great. It was a good first win for our season." Different ways to score the ball key Missouri State's offense was held to just 2-for-12 from behind the 3-point arc. The Lady Bears pivoted and attacked the paint. Throughout the game, Missouri State never pressed offensively. They played to what SeMo gave them, which were easy baskets in the lane. The 3-point shots will fall, but setting a base of attacking the lane will be key in future games for Missouri State. "You'll see the 3-ball eventually this season," Bekemeier said with a smile. "It was just how they guarded us tonight. They were all over us on the perimeter. We were taking what they were giving us." Lady Bears' defensive intensity shines Missouri State forced 18 turnovers, which led to 27 points. The Lady Bears forced the Redhawks to shoot just 26.9% from the field and 20% from behind the arc. item.title: Gilgeous-Alexander leads Thunder past Cavs, Grizzlies beaten
item.description: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's 43-point performance helped Oklahoma City subdue the Cleveland Cavaliers on the road (Jason Miller) Shai Gilgeous-Alexander erupted for 43 points as the Oklahoma City Thunder halted their two-game losing streak with a battling 117-112 road victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday. Oklahoma City had been rocked after suffering a slew of injuries followed by back-to-back 20-point defeats heading into Monday's showdown with last season's Eastern Conference finalists. But a sublime performance from two-time reigning NBA Most Valuable Player Gilgeous-Alexander carried the Thunder to a morale-boosting win at Cleveland's Rocket Arena. Gilgeous-Alexander's 43-point haul came from 14-of-35 shooting from the field with four three-pointers and eight assists. Oklahoma City, missing three starters in Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace, were also boosted by 20 points from Ajay Mitchell and 12 points from Kenrich Williams. Cleveland's points were spread through the line-up, with seven players reaching double figures, including Donovan Mitchell and Meleek Thomas with 17 points apiece. "You never know what the future has in store for you, and all you can do is play the cards you're dealt, that's what we try to do," Gilgeous-Alexander said of the Thunder's response to their injury crisis. "Whatever the game needs we try to play to the best of our ability and come out with a W (win). And tonight we did that." Oklahoma City's victory, which lifts the Thunder to 4-2, launched a packed slate of Monday fixtures across the NBA as the league prepares to take a rest day on Tuesday due to the US mid-term elections. The league's last unbeaten record fell as the Memphis Grizzlies were upset 135-134 at home by the New Orleans Pelicans. Ty Jerome sparked a thrilling late fightback for Memphis with 15 points in the fourth quarter to send the game to overtime, but the Grizzlies rally fell just short. The Philadelphia 76ers improved to 7-1 to stay on top of the Eastern Conference with a 126-107 defeat of the Chicago Bulls. Tyrese Maxey scored 26 points and Jaylen Brown added 25 to guide the Sixers to a fourth consecutive win. V.J. Edgecombe scored 21 points and LeBron James and Joel Embiid added 15 points each. The reigning NBA champion New York Knicks improved to 3-4 with a 103-90 defeat of the Brooklyn Nets at Madison Square Garden. Landry Shamet led the Knicks scoring with 22 points off the bench while Jalen Brunson added 19 points, including four three-pointers. Cade Cunningham's 33-point display helped the Detroit Pistons move to 6-1 with a 124-91 drubbing of the Charlotte Hornets. The Washington Wizards pulled clear of the Orlando Magic 103-94 on the road. The Atlanta Hawks are at 4-4 after a 108-104 defeat of the Indiana Pacers. rcw/pst

Millions know of the viral clip that saw James doing a goofy dance and then hitting the side of the backboard on a three-point attempt prior to the 76ers’ 114-109 win over the Indiana Pacers back on Wednesday. As good as he looks for a 41-year-old professional basketball player, the end is near for his Hall of Fame career, and it certainly seems as though he doesn’t want to take any moment for granted. Grades are based on our usual expectations for each player. Player of the game Evan Mobley 16 points, 7 rebounds, 4 assists, 2 blocks, 2 steal s Kenny Atkinson said before the game that OKC’s defense would swarm the paint and make it difficult to feed the Cleveland bigs. He was right, as Mobley was forced out of the paint for the first three quarters and took roughly half of his shots from the perimeter. It wasn’t until the fourth that Mobley was able to consistently assert himself in the paint. The Cavs found him on the roll multiple times, as he either converted at the rim or earned trips to the free-throw line. It wasn’t enough, but it was a quality adjustment that’s worth noting. Grade: B Grades Donovan Mitchell 17 points, 11 assists, 5 rebounds, 3 turnovers Mitchell struggled with his shot but worked his way to 11 assists by zipping the ball around the floor and being a willing passer. He looked particularly spry in the first quarter, wheeling and dealing without the threat of OKC’s usual perimeter defense. The added playmaking was great and deserves to be mentioned. But, at the end of the day, the Cavs needed more than just 17 points on 17 shots. Grade: B James Harden 14 points, 6 assists, 4 rebounds, 1 turnover Harden has settled into a groove in recent games. His turnovers are down, and his efficiency is on the rise. He shot 5-for-10 from the floor and generated advantages for his teammates throughout the night. item.title: How NDA volleyball swept Bishop Brossart in state tournament opener
item.description: Notre Dame Academy volleyball's narrative over the last few weeks has been to play relaxed after a tough regular season. The Pandas hosted a scrappy Bishop Brossart team in front of a packed gym in Park Hills in the first round of the 2026 state tournament , coming away with a 25-16, 25-20, 25-14 win to advance to Friday evening's state quarterfinals. "Our record – I guess we're 26-11 now – is probably not a record that we're used to but we really did have a strength of schedule and we played a lot of good teams to start the season," Notre Dame co-coach Hannah Colvin said. Notre Dame got out to a fast start, using four runs of at least three points to take a 17-9 lead in the first set. Teagan Kondik, Makayla Roose and Emma Redlinger combined for 13 kills in the set and the Pandas registered five blocks. Brossart came around in the second set, rallying from a 19-14 deficit, thanks to a kill and a block from sophomore Audrey Arnold, forcing NDA to call its lone timeout of the match. The Pandas responded immediately with a Kondik kill and a Grout ace to stretch the lead back to five and held Brossart at bay to close out the set. For all the different looks that Brossart threw at the Pandas with its tall, versatile blockers, NDA was able to mix up the attack thanks to split-second communication from libero Kaia Tilden and setter Ellie Osterkamp. Kondik (13 kills, 16 digs, one block and one ace) and Roose (14 kills, four aces and five blocks) once again led the offense, firing cannonballs into the ground whenever they got the chance, but junior Emma Redlinger was a reliable third option with 10 kills. The junior, along with Ellie Breitling, Sophia Bramlage and Charlotte Verst, has really given the Pandas depth in the postseason and is seeing an increased role this season. "We really just wanted to show up for our team and go all out. We wanted to prove ourselves this year because last year, there were so many good people, but we really wanted to come out and prove ourselves and show that we are on this team for a reason," Redlinger said. One of the most impressive stats of the night was Notre Dame serving nine total aces to just three service errors, winning 57.8 percent of its service points. "We were really just focusing on getting them out of system. Even when they were out of system, they were having to run their outsides a lot and I think that was beneficial for us to not have their middles as involved," Colvin said. The Lady Mustangs got the majority of their production from freshman Evelyn Laker (15 kills) and Audrey Arnold (six kills and a block), limiting senior Callie Ritter to just three kills and a block. Brossart had just 28 kills as a team. item.title: Joe Rogan Reacts to Sketchy Standup by Referee Dan Miragliotta
item.description: Joe Rogan Dan Miragliotta Getty UFC commentator Joe Rogan shared his reaction to the sketchy standup by referee Dan Miragliotta at UFC Vegas 123. Miragliotta stood up Renato Moicano despite having a body triangle and back control against Tom Nolan in the UFC Vegas 123 main event this past Saturday. Despite dominating the fight on the ground, Moicano lost his dominant position when the referees stood the fighters up and was soon after brutally knocked out and finished by Nolan. In Rogan’s opinion, the referee messed up, and he’s worried about what this says for the state of MMA when an official can make a fight-changing decision like this. Joe Rogan Reacts to UFC Vegas 123 Standup UFC commentator Jon Anik shared a text message on his YouTube channel where both men condemned the decision by Miragliotta to stand the fight up between Moicano and Nolan. “If you don’t want to take it from Boston (Jason) Anik, right? Take it from Joe Rogan, who just wait until he cracks a mic on the Joe Rogan Experience and talks about this. He wrote in our text with ‘DC’ (Daniel Cormier), ‘It’s not a sport if refs can do that.’ I’m not sure much else needs to be said,” Anik said (via Bloody Elbow ). Dan Miragliotta Needs to Explain Himself It is in this writer’s opinion that Miragliotta needs to explain himself for his decision to stand Nolan and Moicano up despite the Brazilian having a dominant position and working to finish the fight against Nolan. We rarely see these types of MMA errors where essentially the entire community is in agreement that there was an egregious mistake made. Usually there are at least a few people who play devil’s advocate and see things from the other side of the coin. Although Miragliotta has been one of the top MMA officials for many years, it’s decisions like this one that make people think that he may be better off stepping away and retiring from the sport that he officiates at age 63. item.title: No. 18 Cyclones edged by Tigers 80-76
item.description: SIOUX FALLS, S.D. — A valiant second-half effort fell just short for No. 18 Iowa State on Monday night as the Cyclones dropped their season opener 80-76 to Memphis at the Sanford Pentagon. Despite a dominant performance from Iowa State’s bench and a decisive advantage inside the paint, Memphis leveraged strong perimeter shooting and key late-game execution to pull away in a tightly contested battle featuring 12 lead changes and 11 ties. The Cyclones remained competitive throughout the contest largely due to a massive spark from their reserve unit, which outscored the Tigers’ bench 38-13. Ryan Prather Jr. spearheaded Iowa State’s offensive effort off the bench with a team-high 19 points while connecting on 3 of 6 attempts from beyond the arc. Dominykas Pleta provided highly efficient frontcourt scoring off the pine, contributing 15 points on 7-of-8 shooting from the floor while helping Iowa State establish a 38-26 scoring advantage over Memphis in the paint. Starting forward Tre Singleton notched a double-double with 11 points and 11 rebounds – including six on the offensive glass – and starting guard Tamin Lipsey chipped in 12 points. The primary separation between the two squads came along the perimeter, where Memphis converted 45.0% of its 3-point attempts (9 of 20) compared to just 20.0% (4 of 20) for Iowa State. The Tigers were paced by Jayden Reid’s 26 points and Luke Almodovar’s 18 points, with Memphis also earning an edge at the free-throw line by shooting 25 of 33 (75.8%). Iowa State drew 29 fouls and reached the stripe frequently, knocking down 22 of 32 free throws (68.8%), while holding a narrow 38-36 trailing margin on the glass. After trailing 40-39 at the break, Iowa State continued to exchange blows with Memphis across a tense second half. The Cyclones wiped out a late deficit to knot the score at 69-69 when Prather Jr. sank a pair of free throws with 3:15 remaining. Reid answered with a driving layup to regain the lead for Memphis, but Iowa State stayed within strike distance as Jaquan Johnson sank two free throws to trim the margin to 75-73 with 1:00 left. However, Reid delivered the game’s turning point by hitting a step-in 3-pointer with 38 seconds remaining to push the Tigers ahead by five. Pleta added a late layup with 11 seconds left to pull the Cyclones back within four points, but time expired on Iowa State’s comeback attempt.

Considering he was the one who stayed with the Thunder while Kevin Durant left, Westbrook is the sentimental favorite by far. "Being able to come here and be able to be in Oklahoma City just changed my trajectory of life and how I thought about people. Me and my friends, we always talk about how Oklahoma City has the nicest, and the most kindest people in the world, and I truly believe that," Westbrook said about what the Thunder and the city mean to him . In January, Oklahoma City will get the opportunity to show love to a franchise legend. It will be an emotional January night, but it seems that Westbrook will feel the same as the fans who will be watching in the arena.
